from_notes: Part Number Misattribution: Any option placing Tribunals in Part XI (Relations between Union and States) or Part X (Scheduled & Tribal Areas) is FALSE - It is strictly Part XIV-A.

x: Tribunals are in Part XIV-A (Arts 323-A, 323-B, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976), not Part XI, which deals with Union-State relations. Official Language (XVII), Union Territories (VIII) and Scheduled and Tribal Areas (X) are correctly matched.

from_notes: The CAT exercises original jurisdiction ... Its jurisdiction extends to the All-India Services, the Central civil services, civil posts under the Centre ... They are drawn from both judicial and administrative streams. ... The CAT is not bound by the procedure laid down in the Civil Procedure Code of 1908.
from_notes_src: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch36 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.73-75 (p.73-74); PMF Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.116-118
x: CAT is a statutory body set up in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act, is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, and covers All-India Services, Central services and Central posts. Statement II is wrong: its members come from both judicial and administrative streams.
source: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch36 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.73-75 (p.73-74); PMF Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.116-118

from_notes: Appellate Routes: Telecom/broadcasting/tariff appeals lie directly to the Supreme Court on substantial questions of law; cyber appellate orders route to the High Court.
x: TDSAT orders on telecom, broadcasting and airport tariffs go to the Supreme Court (TRAI Act s.18), while its cyber appellate orders go to the High Court (IT Act s.62) – so both. TRAI cannot hear appeals against TDSAT, which is its appellate body.
evidence: IT Act, 2000 s.62; Finance Act, 2017 (Cyber Appellate Tribunal merged with TDSAT)
dispute: Most books and keys: High Court and Supreme Court. Strictly, in 2003 (the exam year) the only statutory appeal from TDSAT lay to the Supreme Court (TRAI Act s.18); the High Court route came when the Cyber Appellate Tribunal was merged into TDSAT by the Finance Act, 2017.

from_notes: Appeals against NGT orders lie directly to the Supreme Court (within 90 days).
x: Under Section 22 of the NGT Act, 2010 an aggrieved person may appeal to the Supreme Court within 90 days of the NGT's order – directly, not through a High Court.

In the Sundara Kanda of Valmiki's Ramayana, Hanuman kills Ravana's young son Aksha Kumara at the Ashoka grove. Indrajit (Meghanada) was killed by Lakshmana; Mahodara and Mahaparshva were Ravana's commanders, not sons killed by Hanuman.
Judges of the International Court of Justice are elected for nine years (Art. 13, ICJ Statute), a third of the 15 retiring every three years.

x: Under the Government of India Act, 1919 provincial Governors were appointed by the Crown, by convention for five years (the same as the Governor-General); 'six years' has no basis. (The Act itself fixed no term; it was settled by practice.)
